summary.summary: Herefordshire's 2025/26 treasury outturn (Appendix C to Cabinet on 21 May 2026) shows a council running heavily on internal borrowing: its Capital Financing Requirement of £330.8m at 31 March 2026 sits well above external long-term borrowing of £185.1m, though it drew a new £55.0m 10-year loan at 4.83% in the final quarter and flagged more borrowing to come, driven by the capital programme and the ongoing cost of financing its DSG schools deficit (not quantified in this report). Treasury investments stood at £57.1m at a 4.60% average, and investment income of £2.534m beat a £0.552m budget by £1.982m, helped by high-rate short deposits with other local authorities (up to 7.00%). All prudential and treasury indicators were complied with: external debt of £231.2m sat well within the £420m authorised limit, financing costs held at 10% of net revenue, and only 7% of borrowing matures within 12 months. The council also earns about £1.8m a year in loan interest from its waste-disposal PFI provider.

signals.headline: New £55.0m 10-year loan drawn at 4.83% in the final quarter of 2025/26 lifts long-term borrowing to £185.1m at 31 March 2026, with further borrowing flagged for the capital programme and DSG-deficit financing
signals.why: After years of internal borrowing the council is now taking material external long-term debt at above-5% market levels, with more signalled.

signals.headline: The council states its final-quarter 2025/26 borrowing was driven partly by 'the ongoing impact of financing the DSG deficit' (para 4.2); the deficit itself is not quantified in this treasury appendix
signals.why: The schools deficit is converting into real external borrowing need, though its size must be read from the revenue/accounts monitoring rather than this report.

compliance.notes: Strong, comprehensive 2026/27 strategy for a mid-size unitary borrower: full prudential-indicator set with an exemplary 70-year liability benchmark, a robust creditworthiness/investment framework, clear MRP policy and full CIPFA Code adoption. Weakest areas are the commercial/non-treasury disclosure suite (thin, reflecting the council's small ~1% commercial exposure) and a few specific omissions - no distinct fixed/variable interest-rate exposure limits, no quantitative investment risk indicator, no sterling-only or third-party/pension-monies statements.

gaps.evidence: Capital Strategy p.20 references the Prudential Code provision on borrowing in advance of need and the duty to bring an explanation if the council deviates
Capital Strategy p.20 defines and separates service vs commercial investments from treasury; TMS Annex E para 6.3 commits to a schedule of material investments in the accounts
Capital Strategy p.12-14 paras 7.8/8 (scheme selection, due diligence, project-board monitoring) function as de facto investment practices
TMS p.11 Table 14 income dependence 1%; Capital Strategy para 7.8 security/adequate collateral for loans
Capital Strategy p.12 para 7.9 and p.2 para 1.5 (surplus assets recycled or disposed of via the strategic asset management plan)

news_drafts.headline: LEVI programme has approved 14 electric vehicle charging sites but delivered zero installations in Q1, with performance issue attributed to external contractor.
news_drafts.lead: Underperformance against grant-funded programmes affects budget execution and may trigger clawback of funding or conditions on future grants. External partnership delivery risk is relevant to the council's project management oversight.

news_drafts.headline: Capital scheme cost increases and delays evident, including Ross Enterprise Park cost pressures and Buttercross funding drawdown awaiting approval.
news_drafts.lead: Capital scheme cost overruns and delays affect cash flow timing and may indicate budget management or delivery challenges; inability to obtain funding approval delays spending and revenue outcomes.

news_drafts.headline: Home to school transport service moved to in-house delivery from June 2026 to mitigate increasing costs.
news_drafts.lead: Transport is typically a significant council budget line; a decision to move from contractor to in-house delivery to manage costs demonstrates the council is taking material action to address spending pressures.

findings.headline: LEVI programme has approved 14 electric vehicle charging sites but delivered zero installations in Q1, with performance issue attributed to external contractor.
findings.detail: The council reports that 'Herefordshire Council has approved all 14 sites that have been proposed by the contractor, however 0 have been installed'. The council acknowledges 'As socket installation is delivered through external providers the resulting shortfall is beyond our direct control' but states 'Conversations are being held with the provider regarding performance compared to contractual requirements'. This represents a significant delivery shortfall on a funded programme.
findings.matters: Underperformance against grant-funded programmes affects budget execution and may trigger clawback of funding or conditions on future grants. External partnership delivery risk is relevant to the council's project management oversight.
findings.figures: 14 sites approved, 0 installed as at Q1 end.
findings.quote: Herefordshire Council has approved all 14 sites that have been proposed by the contractor, however 0 have been installed. As socket installation is delivered through external providers the resulting shortfall is beyond our direct control.

findings.headline: Capital scheme cost increases and delays evident, including Ross Enterprise Park cost pressures and Buttercross funding drawdown awaiting approval.
findings.detail: Ross Enterprise Park Phase 1 reports that 'costs have increased, these remain within budget' with completion now estimated March 2027 (delayed). The Buttercross Leominster affordable housing refurbishment is delayed pending 'approval of business case to draw down funding', meaning the project cannot spend its allocated budget until approval is received. These reflect cost and schedule pressures across the capital programme.
findings.matters: Capital scheme cost overruns and delays affect cash flow timing and may indicate budget management or delivery challenges; inability to obtain funding approval delays spending and revenue outcomes.
findings.figures: Ross Enterprise Park costs increased; Buttercross completion delayed, pending funding approval.
findings.quote: Although costs have increased, these remain within budget. Completion now estimated March '27. Delays due to change in procurement route, and approval of business case to draw down funding.

findings.headline: Home to school transport service moved to in-house delivery from June 2026 to mitigate increasing costs.
findings.detail: The council has completed its review and implemented a new delivery model, with the service 'launched in June 2026, with expansion due from September 2026 in line with the new academic year'. The original objective explicitly stated the review was designed to 'mitigate increasing costs through a new delivery model'. This represents a material service redesign undertaken to control cost pressures.
findings.matters: Transport is typically a significant council budget line; a decision to move from contractor to in-house delivery to manage costs demonstrates the council is taking material action to address spending pressures.
findings.figures: Costs described as 'increasing' in original objective; no specific costs disclosed.
findings.quote: Service launched in June 2026, with expansion due from September 2026 in line with the new academic year.

findings.headline: PwC commissioned to undertake 12-week savings diagnostic in Community Wellbeing, a high-cost, high-demand service area.
findings.detail: The council has engaged external specialist support specifically to 'identify transformation initiatives in Community Wellbeing to streamline processes, systems, reduce costs, increase revenue, reduce demand, identify alternative efficient ways of working'. The deployment of external expertise to find cost reductions in a high-cost service signals both that material cost pressures exist and that the council is taking active steps to address them.
findings.matters: A council's proactive commissioning of external cost reduction diagnostics signals it is managing financial pressure; the outcome will directly affect medium-term financial resilience.
findings.figures: Community Wellbeing is identified as 'high-cost, high-demand'; diagnostic length is 12 weeks.
findings.quote: 12 week savings diagnostic has been commissioned to be delivered by PwC.

findings.headline: Council is preparing updated MTFS specifically to address an estimated medium-term funding gap.
findings.detail: The council's key action is to 'Prepare an updated Medium Term Financial Strategy (MTFS) which is informed by specific actions to address the estimate funding gap over the medium-term planning period'. The explicit framing of the MTFS as gap-closing indicates the council has identified financial pressures it expects over the medium term and is planning responses.
findings.matters: A lender assessing financial sustainability needs to understand whether a council has identified future funding shortfalls and possesses a credible action plan to close them.
findings.figures: Specific size of the funding gap is not disclosed in this document.
findings.quote: Prepare an updated Medium Term Financial Strategy (MTFS) which is informed by specific actions to address the estimate funding gap over the medium-term planning period
